terra.problem: The passage does not say the trip was long or that Mary entered as if she had been there many times.
The text does not establish where Simeon was during this visit, so it cannot say he was nowhere near the doorway.
The joke mentions tea, which is outside the permitted cookie-making foods and is not in the passage.
The passage does not say whether Elizabeth needed to sit down.
The claim that Luke uses similar words elsewhere needs a reference to that passage.
The oven joke compares its contribution to the great things God did for Mary. Comparisons must stay on the human side of the moment.
Luke 1:26–28 identifies Gabriel and gives his greeting, but the news he brings comes in Luke 1:30–33.
The joke compares the duration of God's mercy to cookies on a cooling rack, rather than keeping the comparison on the human side.
The claim that forty years appears in other Bible stories needs a reference to one of them.

The cookie-tray comparison makes God's bringing down rulers and exalting the humble into the joke. The image also does not clearly work: turning a tray over would not make everything land right side up.
The joke compares God's promise of mercy to Papa Dorin's difficulty keeping a promise about a cookie. Comparisons must stay on the human side.
